paper.title: How well smooth and statsforecast estimate ETS parameters

declarations.competing_interests: The guarantor is the author and maintainer of the smooth package that the study evaluates.

definitions.definition: The ES class of the Python package smooth (Ivan Svetunkov) with the model form fixed; estimated smoothing parameters by likelihood; usual bounds (alpha, beta, gamma in [0,1], beta at most alpha, gamma at most 1 minus alpha); initial states optimised (initial='optimal') or by backcasting (initial='backcasting', its default). Two arms: optimised and backcasting.

The ets_f function of statsforecast (Nixtla) with the model form fixed; likelihood loss (opt_crit 'lik'); smoothing parameters bounded to [0.0001, 0.9999], with beta's upper bound set to the starting alpha (about 0.2 for non-seasonal models); initial states optimised.

Simulated series of length T in {50, 100, 250, 500} from ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) and ETS(A,N,A) with m=12 in innovations form, additive Gaussian errors with sigma=1, l_0=100, b_0=1 and s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12) for j=0,...,11; no burn-in. ETS(A,N,N): $y_t = l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t$, $l_t = l_{t-1} + \alpha \varepsilon_t$. ETS(A,A,N): $y_t = l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t$, $l_t = l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha \varepsilon_t$, $b_t = b_{t-1} + \beta \varepsilon_t$. ETS(A,N,A): $y_t = l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t$, $l_t = l_{t-1} + \alpha \varepsilon_t$, $s_t = s_{t-m} + \gamma \varepsilon_t$; $\varepsilon_t \sim N(0,1)$ i.i.d.
Mean over successful replicates of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Root mean squared error of a smoothing-parameter estimate around its true value, over successful replicates.
Mean absolute error of a smoothing-parameter estimate around its true value, over successful replicates.

5 processes x 4 series lengths x 300 replicates per cell. Each replicate has its own fixed seed derived from the base seed 2026; the three arms are fitted to the same series. Fit failures and non-finite estimates are counted, not dropped.

definitions.term: share of estimates on a bound
definitions.definition: Share of successful replicates whose estimate lies within 0.001 of a bound of the implementation's parameter range: smooth 0 or 1 (beta also at alpha); statsforecast 0.0001 or 0.9999 (beta also at its cap).

claims.statement: For ETS(A,N,A) with $m=12$ and true $\gamma=0.1$ in [[D3:ETS innovations-form data]], [[D1:smooth ES]] estimates $\gamma$ with a bias towards zero for series of 50 to 250 observations, under both initial-state methods.

about.subject: D1
about.relation: estimates the seasonal smoothing parameter with a bias towards zero

scope.conditions: ETS(A,N,A) with m=12, Gaussian errors, series length 50 to 250

assessments.rationale: The result is exploratory, not tested under a plan: one simulation study, with no independent check; one web search found no head-to-head study of these estimators.

claims.statement: For ETS(A,A,N) with true $(\alpha,\beta)=(0.5,0.2)$ in [[D3:ETS innovations-form data]], [[D2:statsforecast ETS]] estimates $\beta$ on its cap in roughly half of replicates at every series length from 50 to 500.

about.subject: D2
about.relation: estimates beta on its cap in a share of replicates

scope.conditions: ETS(A,A,N), Gaussian errors, series length 50 to 500

assessments.rationale: The result is exploratory, not tested under a plan: one simulation study, with no independent check; one web search found no head-to-head study of these estimators.

claims.statement: For non-seasonal ETS in [[D3:ETS innovations-form data]], the RMSE of the estimates of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ from [[D1:smooth ES]] with optimised initial states falls at each series length from 50 to 500.

about.subject: D1
about.relation: has an RMSE for alpha and beta that falls with series length

scope.conditions: ETS(A,N,N) and ETS(A,A,N), Gaussian errors, series length 50 to 500

assessments.rationale: The result is exploratory, not tested under a plan: one simulation study, with no independent check; one web search found no head-to-head study of these estimators.

claims.statement: The errors are i.i.d. $N(0,1)$ and the data are generated exactly by the stated innovations-form ETS model.

evidence.description: Monte Carlo comparison of smoothing-parameter estimates of smooth ES (two initial-state arms) and statsforecast ets_f on simulated ETS data (definitions D3 and D7). The bias, RMSE and MAE come from lab run RN4 (analyse.py --output error) and the share on a bound from RN3 (analyse.py), both over the replicate file of RN2 (simulate.py --seed 2026 --reps 300). The lab record holds all runs; every result is in files/ets-param-recovery.results.csv. All 18,000 fits succeeded.
evidence.model: ETS innovations-form models of definition D3, with m=12 for ETS(A,N,A)
evidence.seeds: base seed 2026; replicate seed 2026*10^7 + p*10^6 + T_index*10^5 + replicate (p process, T_index length, replicate 0 to 299)

execution.notes: Scripts simulate.py and analyse.py in claimset-code/ets-param-recovery/.

tables.description: Bias, RMSE and MAE of the smoothing-parameter estimates of successful fits, and the share of estimates on a bound, for 5 processes, 4 series lengths and 3 arms, 300 replicates per cell (lab runs RN4 and RN3); values to four significant digits
